rules.name: Definite-time registrations combine date and clock time in UTC
rules.plainEnglish: When the input type is 'definite time', on submit the app merges the From/To date with the Start/End time fields into full UTC date-times before sending.
rules.given: InputType = DefiniteTime, FromDate '2025-03-10T00:00:00', ToDate '2025-03-10T00:00:00', Start time 08:30:00, End time 12:00:00
rules.then: FromDate is sent as '2025-03-10T08:30:00' and ToDate as '2025-03-10T12:00:00'
rules.parameters: UTC calendar, locale-invariant date-time and HH:mm:ss formatters
rules.edgeCases: End time earlier than start time on the same day is not rejected on the client. Parsing failure of any of the four values sends empty strings.
rules.suspectedDefect: If any of the four values fails to parse, FromDate and ToDate are overwritten with empty strings and submitted, silently wiping the dates instead of blocking the save.

rules.name: Balances cover the whole calendar month
rules.plainEnglish: The balances overview is requested from the first to the last day of the month being viewed.
rules.given: The calendar shows February 2024
rules.then: Balances are requested for 2024-02-01 to 2024-02-29
rules.edgeCases: The month is the one currently displayed in list or month view, else the current month (CalendarContainerViewController 401-408).

rules.name: Days on or before the confirmation date are marked confirmed or approved
rules.plainEnglish: In the month grid, a day is marked time-confirmed when it is on or before the confirmed entry's date, and time-approved when it is on or before the approved entry's date.
rules.given: A confirmed entry dated 2026-09-15 and an approved entry dated 2026-09-10
rules.then: 1-15 September are marked confirmed and 1-10 September are also marked approved. 16 September has no mark.
rules.parameters: Comparison: date <= eventDate, or the same calendar day

rules.name: List calendar groups by UTC month, newest first, without duplicates
rules.plainEnglish: List items are placed into sections by their start date's UTC year and month. An absence whose id is already in its section is skipped. Items in each section are sorted newest first, and sections are ordered newest month first (SectionsSingleSourceCalendarViewModel.swift:64-66).
rules.given: Absence id 'A1' dated 2026-09-01T00:30+02:00 arriving twice in two pages
rules.then: A1 appears once, in the August 2026 section, because the start date is 2026-08-31 in UTC.
rules.parameters: Month key: getUTCYearMonth(). Items without a date go under distantPast.

rules.name: Each team member gets one yearly all-day birthday event with a reminder the day before
rules.plainEnglish: For every employee in the manager's employee list without an existing birthday event (matched by employee id stored in the event URL, looking 10 years ahead), the app creates a yearly repeating all-day event on the date of birth in the current year, with an alarm 1440 minutes (1 day) before.
rules.given: Employee id E1 born 1990-03-15, no event with url E1 in the next 10 years, today 2026-09-28
rules.then: An all-day yearly event starting 2026-03-15 is saved with an alarm 1 day before, and E1 is added to the synced list
rules.parameters: Lookahead 10 years; recurrence yearly, interval 1; alarm -1440 minutes; allDay true
rules.suspectedDefect: Start date uses moment.utc(dateOfBirth).set('year', currentYear) then UTC start of day: Feb 29 births clamp to Feb 28 permanently; UTC midnight on an all-day event may shift the day in negative-offset time zones. Also employees added later are only synced when the switch is toggled again.
rules.question: Is it intended that a 29 February birthday is stored on 28 February (moment clamps the date in non-leap 2026) and then repeats on 28 Feb every year, and that dates are computed in UTC, which can show the event one day early in time zones west of UTC?

rules.name: Sickness summaries default to today's date in UTC
rules.plainEnglish: The sick-child current-year summary (and the self-certification 12-month summary at lines 357-366) uses today's UTC date as the target date when none is given.
rules.given: A device in Oslo (UTC+2) at 2026-09-29 01:00 local time and no target date
rules.then: targetisodate=2026-09-28 (the previous day) is sent
rules.suspectedDefect: new Date().toISOString() gives the UTC date, so between local midnight and the UTC offset the counts are for yesterday; the sick-child call reuses details=sickness12months, which looks copy-pasted.
rules.question: Should the target date be the user's local date? And is details=sickness12months also correct for the sick-child current-year summary?

rules.name: Balance group total shown as expandable row
rules.plainEnglish: When a balance group has a total, it is shown as one row with the total and unit that expands to the individual balances; without a total, balances are listed directly.
rules.given: A vacation group total 25 days with balances 'Earned 20' and 'Transferred 5'
rules.then: One row '25 days' expands to 'Earned 20 days' and 'Transferred 5 days'
rules.edgeCases: The total is shown as given by the server; the app does not recompute it.

rules.name: Confirmed-time entry is added to a month even when the feed had none
rules.plainEnglish: If the month's feed items include no confirmed-time entry, the app fetches the confirmation details and puts their entries at the front of the month's items. The grid can then mark confirmed days.
rules.given: A September 2026 feed with 3 absences and no confirm-time entry, and confirmation details with confirmer date 2026-08-31
rules.then: A 'Timesheet confirmed' entry dated 2026-08-31 is added to the grid items.

rules.name: Weekend is always Saturday and Sunday
rules.plainEnglish: The grid treats weekday 1 (Sunday) and weekday 7 (Saturday) as weekend days in every locale. Hide-weekends removes the Saturday and Sunday column names (lines 156-161).
rules.given: A user whose locale has a Friday-Saturday weekend
rules.then: Saturday and Sunday are hidden. Friday stays visible.
rules.question: Should weekends come from the company's work calendar or the locale rather than a fixed Saturday and Sunday?

rules.name: Month grid starts on the locale's first weekday and has just enough rows
rules.plainEnglish: The grid starts on the calendar's first weekday on or before the 1st of the month. The number of weeks is the offset plus the days in the month, divided by 7 and rounded up.
rules.given: September 2026 (1 September is a Tuesday) in a locale where weeks start on Monday
rules.then: It starts on Monday 31 August and has (1 + 30 + 6) / 7 = 5 rows, ending Sunday 4 October.
rules.parameters: Fallbacks: 6 weeks if the month interval is unknown; 30 days if the month length is unknown

rules.name: Multi-day absences are detected in GMT
rules.plainEnglish: An absence counts as multi-day when its start and end fall on different calendar days in GMT, whatever the user's time zone.
rules.when: The app checks whether it spans several days
rules.then: It counts as multi-day, and the short date period is added to its description.

rules.name: Hour-based absence duration falls back to end minus start
rules.plainEnglish: For hour-based absences, the duration comes from the 'hours' property, parsed as a localized number and multiplied by 3600 seconds. If the property is missing or not a number, the app uses the time between start and end. The result is formatted as a compact duration in the device locale.
rules.given: An Hours absence with hours='7,5' in a nb-NO locale, and another with no hours property running 09:00-11:30
rules.then: The first shows a compact 7 h 30 min. The second shows a compact 2 h 30 min.

rules.name: Confirmed-time row joins the list only inside the loaded date range
rules.plainEnglish: The confirmed-time row is added to the list once, when its date falls between the loaded minimum and maximum dates, or when no more pages remain in the direction that covers it.
rules.given: Loaded range 2026-06-01..2026-09-30 and a confirmation dated 2026-09-15
rules.then: The 'Timesheet confirmed' row is added under September 2026 and is not added again later.

rules.name: Each team member gets one yearly all-day work anniversary event with a reminder the day before
rules.plainEnglish: Same as birthdays but based on the employment date, stored in the anniversaries calendar.
rules.given: Employee id E2 with employmentDate 2015-06-01 and no existing anniversary event
rules.then: An all-day yearly event starting 2026-06-01 with a 1-day-before alarm is saved in 'Manager App - Anniversaries'
rules.parameters: Lookahead 10 years; recurrence yearly; alarm -1440 minutes
rules.suspectedDefect: Same Feb 29 / UTC start-of-day issue as birthdays.

rules.name: Claims status filter applies to both past and future pages, split at today
rules.plainEnglish: When one or more claim statuses are selected, the past feed starts from today and the future feed from tomorrow, both limited to the selected statuses. When no status is selected, the default feed URLs are kept.
rules.given: Today is 2026-09-28 and the user selects the 'approved' quick filter
rules.then: past claims load from 2026-09-28 backwards and future claims from 2026-09-29 forwards, both with status 'approved'
rules.parameters: past anchor = today; future anchor = today + 1 day
rules.edgeCases: An empty selection skips the URL rewrite, so all statuses are shown.

rules.name: Duplicate claims are removed by claim id
rules.plainEnglish: A claim that arrives again (for example from both the empty-claims fetch and the paged fetch) is shown once, matched by id. Claims without an id are never treated as duplicates.
rules.given: Claim id 'C-100' has already been listed in 2026, and the next page returns 'C-100' again
rules.then: 'C-100' appears only once
rules.edgeCases: If both ids are nil, the claims count as different, so id-less claims can repeat.

rules.name: Registration templates, time templates and dimension values fail when the server status is Error
rules.plainEnglish: Calendar templates are accepted only when the server status exists, is not Error, and data is present. Otherwise the server's status text is shown as a validation error, or a generic error when there is no text.
rules.given: The templates endpoint returns status Error with description 'No employment in period'
rules.when: the user opens registration for 2026-10-01 to 2026-10-31
rules.then: the user sees the validation error 'No employment in period'
rules.edgeCases: A missing status object also counts as failure. getTimeTemplates (TimeService.swift:79-101) and getDimensionsValues (lines 115-134) use the same pattern.

rules.name: Calendar feed keeps only Absence-type items
rules.plainEnglish: When loading calendar items for a date range, only items of type 'Absence' are kept (this type also carries attendance and supplement item types). Any other item type is dropped. The end date defaults to today.
rules.given: The calendar endpoint returns an 'Absence' item and an item of type 'Payslip' for September 2026
rules.then: only the Absence item is returned
rules.parameters: CalendarItemFamily discriminator 'type': Absence → CalendarItemAbsence; anything else is unknown and dropped
rules.edgeCases: A paged feed (getCalendarItems(url:), lines 43-55) fails unless the first status is Success.

rules.name: Empty option values are sent as null
rules.plainEnglish: When a registration is saved, an option value left as an empty string is sent to the server as null.
rules.given: An Hours option whose value field is ''
rules.then: the JSON contains value: null

rules.name: Absence from and to dates accept date-only or date-time
rules.plainEnglish: The FromDate and ToDate fields of an absence are read as a UTC date, falling back to a UTC date-time. The summary formatter instead uses only 'yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss' in GMT.
rules.given: FromDate value '2026-10-05'
rules.when: dateFrom / the summary formatter's fromDate is read
rules.then: dateFrom is 2026-10-05, but the summary formatter's fromDate is nil, so no date is shown
rules.parameters: field ids FromDate, ToDate; the formatter parse lives at AbsenceTypeFormatStyle.swift:514-524
rules.suspectedDefect: Two different parsers for the same field: a date-only value is shown by one path and silently dropped by the other.
rules.question: Does the server ever send FromDate/ToDate as date-only for predicted registrations?

rules.name: Confirm-time date validations: the rule name says when the date fails
rules.plainEnglish: The date chosen for confirming time is checked against server rules. GreaterThan X is valid only on or before X, GreaterThanOrEqual X only before X, LessThan X only on or after X, LessThanOrEqual X only after X. Required uses a regex.
rules.given: The server sends a GreaterThan validation with value '2026-09-30' at level Error
rules.then: 2026-10-01 fails with the server's displayText, and 2026-09-30 is valid
rules.parameters: validation types RegEx/Required, Object/GreaterThan, GreaterThanOrEqual, LessThan, LessThanOrEqual; levels Error and Warning; dates in Constants.dateFormatter format
rules.edgeCases: An unparseable date or a missing value counts as invalid. Unknown type and name pairs decode to nil and are ignored. The base validation always passes.
rules.suspectedDefect: The names describe the failing condition (inverted from the usual meaning). Rebuilders may implement it the other way round. Confirming time beyond the allowed date affects payroll.
rules.question: Does the server define 'GreaterThan X' as 'error when the date is greater than X'? The client assumes so.

rules.name: Confirm-time: first failing validation at a given level
rules.plainEnglish: For the chosen date, the app finds the first validation on the 'Date' field that fails at the requested level (Error or Warning), so Error and Warning can be handled separately.
rules.given: The Date field has a Warning LessThan '2026-09-01' and an Error GreaterThan '2026-09-30'
rules.when: the user picks 2026-08-15 and the Error level is checked
rules.then: there is no Error failure; checking the Warning level returns the LessThan warning

rules.name: Medical certificate percentage 0-100 in 5% steps, default 100%
rules.plainEnglish: The certificate percentage stepper ranges from 0 to 100 in steps of 5, starts at 100 and is displayed with a percent sign.
rules.given: A certificate percentage of 100
rules.when: The user taps minus three times
rules.then: It reads '85%' and the value 85 is stored
rules.edgeCases: A stored value outside 0-100 is ignored and 100 is shown. Fractions are truncated with Int().

rules.name: Hours/percent number entry capped at 999
rules.plainEnglish: The hours or percent entry field accepts only numeric input whose value does not exceed 999, and clears its content when the user starts editing.
rules.given: An empty Hours field
rules.then: The field shows '100'; the 4th digit is rejected because 1000 > 999
rules.edgeCases: Percent is not capped at 100 here. Deletions are always allowed.
rules.suspectedDefect: The check appends the typed character to the end of the text rather than applying it at the cursor range, so edits in the middle are validated against the wrong number; also a percent above 100 (e.g. 250) is accepted client-side.

rules.name: Comment text is cleared when the user starts editing
rules.plainEnglish: The text field is meant to clear only its placeholder when focused, but because placeholder and real text share the same colour, any existing text is cleared on focus.
rules.given: An existing absence with comment 'Dentist 10:00'
rules.when: The user taps into the comment field to edit
rules.then: The field is emptied; if they type 'x' the saved comment becomes 'x'
rules.edgeCases: If the user leaves without typing, the model keeps the old value.
rules.suspectedDefect: Placeholder check compares against the normal text colour, so real comments are wiped on focus (data loss risk).
rules.question: Is clearing an existing comment on focus intended, or should only the placeholder be cleared?

rules.name: Unrecognised date in template falls back to today
rules.plainEnglish: Date fields accept 'yyyy-MM-dd' or a date-time string; if neither parses, the picker shows today and an error is logged, but the stored value is not changed.
rules.given: A template FromDate value '10/03/2025'
rules.then: The date row shows today's date while the model still holds '10/03/2025'
rules.suspectedDefect: Displayed date and submitted value can differ.

rules.name: To-date follows from-date and cannot be earlier
rules.plainEnglish: When the user picks a new from-date, the to-date is reset to the same day, its picker minimum becomes the from-date, the available absence types are reloaded for the new period and all chosen cost-unit dimension values are cleared.
rules.given: A registration with FromDate 2025-03-10, ToDate 2025-03-14 and Project dimension '1001'
rules.then: ToDate becomes 2025-03-17, dates before 2025-03-17 cannot be picked for ToDate, templates are re-fetched for 17-17 March and the Project dimension is emptied
rules.edgeCases: Picking the same date again does not trigger (DateTableViewCell only fires when value changes). If the new period returns zero templates, the old type list is kept.

rules.name: Definite-time adds required start and end time fields prefilled from the dates
rules.plainEnglish: Selecting the 'definite time' input type relabels the from-date as 'Date' and adds required Start time and End time fields, prefilled from the time part of the from/to values (or the last value the user entered).
rules.given: FromDate '2025-03-10T09:00:00' and ToDate '2025-03-10T15:00:00' and no cached times
rules.when: The input type DefiniteTime is shown
rules.then: Start time shows 09:00 and End time 15:00, both required
rules.edgeCases: If dates are date-only strings, parsing fails and current device time is used as default.

rules.name: Save is disabled until every required field has a value
rules.plainEnglish: The Save button on the absence/time registration form is enabled only when no field marked required by the server template is empty.
rules.given: A Vacation template whose fields FromDate (required, '2025-03-10') and Comment (required, empty)
rules.when: The form re-evaluates after any field change
rules.then: Save is disabled; once Comment is 'Family trip' Save becomes enabled
rules.parameters: required flag comes from server template fieldInfo; check is value.isEmpty
rules.edgeCases: Only top-level fieldInfo is checked; the client-added Start/End time fields and dimension sub-fields are not validated. A whitespace-only value counts as filled.
rules.suspectedDefect: Required dimension sub-items (Dimensions.items) are never checked, so a required cost unit can be left empty on the client.

rules.name: Certificate fields stripped on submit when no certificate
rules.plainEnglish: When creating a registration with the medical certificate switch off, certificate date and percentage are blanked before sending.
rules.given: A Sickness registration where the certificate percentage was set to 50 and then the switch turned off
rules.when: The user saves a new registration
rules.then: Certificate date and percentage are sent empty
rules.edgeCases: The same stripping is not done on update (submitUpdatedEvent), relying on the switch handler having cleared them.
rules.suspectedDefect: Update path does not re-clear certificate fields; values restored by the section cache could be sent on edit.

rules.name: Child field defaults to the first child
rules.plainEnglish: For absence types with a Child field (e.g. sick child), an empty child value is preset to the first child in the list.
rules.given: A Sick child template with children ['Emma', 'Liam'] and no selection
rules.then: Child is set to 'Emma'
rules.edgeCases: A user who does not notice may register for the wrong child.

rules.name: Medical certificate section applies only to sickness and is cleared when switched off
rules.plainEnglish: For Sickness only, a 'medical certificate' switch controls the certificate date and percentage: on restores the last entered values (date defaults to the from-date, percentage to 100), off clears both.
rules.given: A Sickness registration from 2025-03-10 with no cached certificate values
rules.when: The user turns the medical certificate switch on
rules.then: Certificate date is 2025-03-10 and certificate percentage is 100; turning it off empties both
rules.edgeCases: Ignored for any event type other than Sickness. When the switch is off only the toggle row is shown.

rules.name: Tapping the selected dimension value clears it
rules.plainEnglish: Selecting a dimension value sets it; selecting the already-selected value deselects it and empties the dimension.
rules.given: Project dimension currently '1001 - Internal'
rules.then: The Project dimension becomes empty
rules.parameters: recently used values sorted by id (71-87)
rules.edgeCases: Recently used list is sorted by id string, not by recency.

rules.name: Confirming time from the day sheet: errors block, warnings need user approval
rules.plainEnglish: Before confirming time up to a date, the app fetches the confirm-time template for that date. A failing validation at Error level stops the confirmation and shows its message. A failing Warning-level validation asks the user; if they press OK, the app confirms without re-checking any validation.
rules.given: The user taps Confirm time on 2026-09-15 and the template returns a failing Warning 'You have 2 unregistered days'
rules.when: The user presses OK in the warning alert
rules.then: The time confirmation is registered for 2026-09-15 through the template's update link (DayDetailFeature.swift:109-118). With an Error-level failure, an Error alert shows its text and nothing is registered.
rules.parameters: Validation levels: Error, then Warning. Fallback message: 'unexpectedError'. The update link rel is .update.
rules.suspectedDefect: If the template has no update link, registerTimeConfirmation is called with url=nil, and the app does not check for that first.

rules.name: Sick leave missing a required medical certificate date cannot be confirmed directly
rules.plainEnglish: A predicted Sickness absence is not ready to confirm when its 'Certificate.Date' field is required and empty. The user must edit it first. All other predictions are ready (EventDataType.swift:79-94).
rules.given: The agent predicts sickness from 2026-09-14, with Certificate.Date required and empty
rules.then: No Confirm button is offered for it. The bot says a medical certificate is required for the absence from 14.09.2026, with buttons 'Edit registration' and 'Cancel'.
rules.parameters: Field id 'Certificate.Date'; event type Sickness; the date is formatted numeric in the current locale.

rules.name: Employee Agent confirms the timesheet without checking template validations
rules.plainEnglish: When the user confirms a timesheet predicted by the agent, the app reads the date from the template's Date field and registers the confirmation through the template's update link. It does not evaluate any Error or Warning validations first.
rules.given: The agent predicts 'confirm time up to 2026-09-15', and the template carries a failing Warning validation
rules.then: The confirmation is sent at once, with no warning shown. On success the chat reads 'timesheet sent for approval'. On failure an error message appears.
rules.parameters: The date is parsed with Constants.dateFormatter. Missing data gives unexpectedError id 04e45a6c-268e-41bc-8be9-53a13354c907.
rules.suspectedDefect: This path skips the validation gate that the day-sheet path enforces. It also parses the date with Constants.dateFormatter, while the event description (CalendarBotEventDescription.swift:28) parses the same field with utcDateFormatter, so the date shown and the date submitted can differ across time zones.
rules.question: Should confirming through the agent apply the same Error and Warning checks as the calendar's Confirm time, or does the prediction service already check them?

rules.name: Device calendar permission is required before syncing
rules.plainEnglish: If the app does not have calendar permission, it asks for it; if the user refuses, it shows a 'missing calendar permissions' error and stops without changing anything.
rules.given: Calendar permission status is 'denied'
rules.when: A sync is started and the user refuses the permission prompt
rules.then: An error toast 'missing-calendar-permissions' is shown and the sync is aborted (returns false)

rules.name: Employee calendar requires the employee's company tenant
rules.plainEnglish: The calendar can load only when the employee is found in the cached employee list with a company tenant id; otherwise, once loading is done, it shows the load error message.
rules.given: Employee id E9 is not in the cached employee list and the list has finished loading
rules.then: The screen shows 'employee_calendar_load_error' and no feed is requested

rules.name: Workshift company setting defaults to time mode, and shifts without a parseable start are dropped
rules.plainEnglish: A roster shift is kept only if its local start time parses. Its id is 'roster-' plus the start time. If the server sends no data, the app assumes no shifts and time (not hours) mode.
rules.given: A shift with startLocal '2026-01-02T08:00:00' and one with no startLocal
rules.then: one shift with id 'roster-2026-01-02T08:00:00' is kept and the other is dropped
rules.parameters: default WorkshiftResponse(useWorkshiftsInHours: false, workshifts: []) at CalendarService.swift:87
rules.edgeCases: Local times are parsed with a UTC formatter, so they display correctly only if the display also uses UTC. Two shifts with the same start get the same id.
rules.question: Can two roster shifts start at the same time (split shifts)? The id would collide.

rules.name: Dimension (cost unit) search sends the search term as query 'q'
rules.plainEnglish: Searching cost-unit dimension values adds the typed term to the server-provided link as the query parameter 'q'.
rules.given: A dimension values link and the search term 'Oslo'
rules.then: the link is called with q=Oslo
rules.parameters: searchParam = "q"; DimensionValueDefaults count = 50 and offset = 0 are declared but not used in this service
rules.suspectedDefect: DimensionValueDefaults (50/0) is dead code, so the page size is whatever the server link contains.

rules.name: Special days: unparseable dates dropped, public-holiday flag ignored
rules.plainEnglish: Special days are shown by date and name. Entries whose date is not an ISO date are dropped, and the server's isPublicHoliday flag is not passed on.
rules.given: The server returns {date:'2026-12-25', displayName:'Christmas Day', isPublicHoliday:true} and {date:'25/12', displayName:'X'}
rules.then: one special day, 25 Dec 2026 'Christmas Day', is kept, with no holiday flag
rules.question: Should public holidays be shown differently from other special days? The client currently discards isPublicHoliday.

rules.name: Employee Agent rejects an empty prompt
rules.plainEnglish: A prompt to the Employee Agent must not be empty. The prompt is sent with the device's current local time and time zone offset, so the server can resolve words like 'tomorrow'.
rules.given: The user sends '' / 'Vacation tomorrow' at 2026-09-28 10:00 in UTC+2
rules.then: '' fails with 'Invalid input. Input cannot be empty'; 'Vacation tomorrow' is posted with localTime '2026-09-28T10:00:00+02:00'
rules.edgeCases: A prompt of only spaces passes the check. The error text is hard-coded in English (CalendarBotService.swift:66-68).
rules.suspectedDefect: No whitespace trim, so ' ' is sent to the server. The error message is not localized.

rules.name: Checkout template date range is set only when the link supports it
rules.plainEnglish: When opening the checkout template for a date range, the from and to dates are written into the link only if it already has both fromDate and toDate parameters (matched case-insensitively). Otherwise the link is used unchanged.
rules.given: A checkout template link with FromDate and ToDate parameters, and a range from 2026-09-28 to 2026-09-28
rules.then: FromDate=2026-09-28&ToDate=2026-09-28 is set on the link

rules.name: Template lookup by event type short code
rules.plainEnglish: To start a registration of a given type, the app takes the first template across all groups whose short code matches.
rules.given: Groups 'Absence' and 'Time', both holding a template with short code 'FER'
rules.then: the template from the first group is used

rules.name: Month/year picker spans 20 years back and forward
rules.plainEnglish: The month/year picker offers years from 20 before to 20 after the shown year and jumps to the 1st of the chosen month; arrows and swipes move one month.
rules.given: The calendar shows March 2025
rules.then: Years 2005-2045 are offered; choosing June 2030 shows 1 June 2030
rules.edgeCases: Header reads abbreviated month and year, e.g. 'Mar 2025'.

rules.name: Blank or overlapping agent prompts are ignored
rules.plainEnglish: A prompt is sent to the agent only if it still has text after trimming whitespace and no other agent task is running. Sending also stops voice recording and clears any quick-response buttons still on screen.
rules.given: The prompt field holds ' ', or a previous prediction is still loading
rules.when: The user presses send or the return key
rules.then: Nothing is sent. The prompt ' sick today ' would be sent as 'sick today'.

rules.name: Month/year picker offers 2 years back and 5 years forward
rules.plainEnglish: The year dropdown lists from 2 years before to 5 years after the year shown; month names come from the app language, capitalised; a pick jumps to the first of that month.
rules.given: The grid shows September 2026
rules.when: The user opens the year dropdown
rules.then: Years 2024 to 2031 are listed
rules.suspectedDefect: The range is relative to the displayed year, not today's year, so it does not really limit navigation.
rules.question: Should the year range be fixed to today's year? It is based on the year shown, so repeated picks (and the arrows) can reach any year, while the list view is capped at 24 months back.

rules.name: Claims tab and its filter bar appear only when the claims data source is enabled
rules.plainEnglish: Claims are fetched, and the quick filter bar is shown, only when the claims data source reports that it is enabled.
rules.given: claimsPagingController.dataSource.isEnabled is false for this user
rules.then: no claims are fetched and no status filter bar is shown
rules.parameters: isEnabled comes from ClaimsPagingControllerDataSource (flag defined outside this area)
rules.edgeCases: The filter bar gate is in ClaimsCalendarViewModel+UIKit.swift:13-14.
rules.question: What decides dataSource.isEnabled (a company setting, role or feature flag)? The target app has to reproduce it.

rules.name: Payslips list filtered by selected employers (tenants)
rules.plainEnglish: When the user picks employers, the payslip list is cleared and reloaded with only those tenant ids. Past payslips load from today and future ones from tomorrow.
rules.given: The user has payslips from tenants 'T1' and 'T2' and selects only 'T1', today being 2026-09-28
rules.then: the list resets and loads only T1 payslips, past ones from 2026-09-28 backwards and future ones from 2026-09-29
rules.parameters: past anchor = today; future anchor = today + 1 day

rules.name: Start-page absence cards: which vacation and parental leave items become cards
rules.plainEnglish: Only vacation and parental leave items that have both a start and end date become start-page cards: declined vacation starting today or later, approved parental leave that is upcoming or ongoing, and approved vacation that is ongoing, upcoming within 14 days, or approved further ahead.
rules.given: Today is 2026-09-28 and the calendar returns an approved Vacation from 2026-10-05 to 2026-10-09, an approved Vacation from 2026-11-02 to 2026-11-06, a denied Vacation from 2026-09-28, and an approved Sickness item
rules.when: the start page builds its absence cards
rules.then: the 5 Oct vacation shows as an Upcoming Vacation card, the 2 Nov vacation as an Approved Vacation card, the 28 Sep denied vacation as a Declined Vacation card, and the sickness item gets no card
rules.parameters: twoWeeksInFuture = today + 14 days; statuses 'approved', 'denied'; item types Vacation, ParentalLeave; comparisons at day granularity
rules.edgeCases: An approved vacation starting exactly on day today+14 matches neither the 'before today+14' nor the 'after today+14' branch, so it gets no card. Items without dateFrom or dateTo are dropped. Pending vacations never get a card.
rules.suspectedDefect: Gap at the 14-day boundary: a vacation starting exactly 14 days ahead gets no card. AppConstants.CardExpiration values are static lets, so they are computed once, the first time they are used. If the app stays running past midnight, the window stays anchored to the launch day.

rules.name: Absences are edited or deleted only through server-provided links
rules.plainEnglish: An absence can be updated only if the server sent an 'update' link, and deleted only if it sent a 'delete' link. Without the link, the action fails with an unexpected error.
rules.given: An approved vacation whose detail response has only a 'self' link
rules.when: the user tries to edit or delete it
rules.then: no request is sent and an unexpected error is raised
rules.edgeCases: This also covers CAP-016 (delete). Edit permission depends entirely on the server links; the client has no status check of its own.

rules.name: Deleting a check-in uses the server's link and HTTP method
rules.plainEnglish: A check-in can be deleted or updated only through a server-provided action with a non-empty link. Delete also needs a valid HTTP method.
rules.given: A check-in action with href '' / a valid href and method 'delete'
rules.then: an empty href raises an error and no call is made; a valid href is called with DELETE
rules.parameters: method is upper-cased and mapped to HTTPMethod

rules.name: Time confirmation and its template: HTTP 403 means the feature is off
rules.plainEnglish: If the server answers 403 to the confirm-time details or template request, the app treats time confirmation as disabled for this user rather than as an error. Any status other than Success returns the server's message.
rules.given: The user's company has not enabled time confirmation
rules.then: the result is featureDisabled (CalendarError / AbsenceRegistrationError) and no error message is shown

rules.name: Editing a checkout should require both update and delete links (unused check)
rules.plainEnglish: A validation that a checkout has both update and delete links exists but is never called, so the edit screen opens regardless.
rules.given: A checkout template with no update or delete links
rules.then: The edit screen opens anyway; errors only appear when saving or deleting
rules.suspectedDefect: verifyInputData is dead code; start() never calls it.
rules.question: Should the edit check-in screen refuse to open (invalidInputData) when the update or delete link is missing, as verifyInputData intends?

rules.name: Check-in edit and delete need server links
rules.plainEnglish: A check-in/check-out registration can be updated only if the server supplied an 'update' link and deleted only if it supplied a 'delete' link; otherwise an unexpected error is shown.
rules.given: A checkout template whose links contain update but not delete
rules.then: An unexpected error is shown and nothing is deleted
rules.edgeCases: The Delete button is still displayed because edit mode is set regardless of links.

rules.name: Absence types reload only with calendar write permission
rules.plainEnglish: Absence/time templates for a new period are fetched only if the user has calendar write permissions; without them an empty list is used and the current type is kept.
rules.given: A user without calendar write permission
rules.then: No templates are requested and the form stays unchanged
rules.edgeCases: Missing company features throws unexpected error F3E6C9B3-7284-4F9B-8BAA-E5859750CC57.

rules.name: Changing check-out dates requires time permissions
rules.plainEnglish: When the date of a check-out edit changes, a fresh check-out template is fetched only if the company grants the user Add time or Time write; otherwise nothing is reloaded.
rules.given: A user whose company features are [absenceRead] editing a check-out
rules.then: No new template is fetched and the form keeps the old template
rules.edgeCases: A server error with no data shows the status description or 'Unexpected error' and pops the screen.

rules.name: Input type selector only shown when more than one option exists
rules.plainEnglish: The day/hours/percent segmented selector appears only if the template offers several input types; the stored choice is used if still offered, otherwise the first option is selected, and choosing Hours or Percent adds a numeric field for that option.
rules.given: A template with input type options FullDay, Hours, Percent and a stored value 'Hours'
rules.then: The selector shows three segments with Hours selected and an hours number field is added
rules.parameters: option dataType decimal or percent adds a field
rules.edgeCases: A single-option input type is hidden entirely; a stored value no longer offered is replaced by option 1 and written back to the model.

rules.name: Confirm-time entry offered only with confirm-time permission
rules.plainEnglish: The type picker for a new registration includes the 'confirm timesheet' item only when the company grants confirm-time permission.
rules.given: A user whose company lacks the confirmTime feature
rules.when: They open 'Select type' from the calendar
rules.then: Only absence/time templates are listed, no timesheet confirmation
rules.edgeCases: Templates are fetched for the initial date range (default today-today).

rules.name: Edit button shown only when server provides edit links; edit needs write permission
rules.plainEnglish: On an absence's detail screen, Edit appears only if the server returned edit links, and tapping it opens the editor only if calendar templates can be loaded (requires calendar write permission and at least one template).
rules.given: An approved vacation whose detail response has links, viewed by a user without calendar write permission
rules.then: The spinner closes and the editor does not open
rules.edgeCases: No message explains why editing did nothing.
rules.suspectedDefect: Silent no-op when templates are empty; the user gets no feedback.

rules.name: Tapping a calendar day: register on empty day, details otherwise
rules.plainEnglish: In month view, tapping a day with no entries starts a new registration for that day only if the user has calendar write permission; a day with entries opens the day detail sheet.
rules.given: A user without calendar write permission and an empty 12 March
rules.then: Nothing opens; tapping 13 March with a vacation opens day details
rules.edgeCases: Taps while dragging are ignored.

rules.name: Long-press and drag registers a period
rules.plainEnglish: Long-pressing and dragging across days selects a date range (in either direction) and on release starts a registration for that period if the user has write permission; only days in the displayed month can be selected.
rules.given: A user with write permission in March 2025
rules.when: They long-press 14 March and drag back to 10 March
rules.then: A new registration opens from 10 to 14 March
rules.edgeCases: The range can include weekends even when weekends are hidden.

rules.name: Roster shifts cannot be opened as registrations
rules.plainEnglish: In day details, tapping a roster shift does nothing; other entries open their registration; 'Register' in day details requires write permission.
rules.given: Day details for 12 March with a roster shift 08:00-15:00
rules.then: Nothing opens

rules.name: Day detail sheet: which actions appear and how events are listed
rules.plainEnglish: The day sheet shows a special day as a red header (named 'Special day' when it has no name). Roster shifts appear as non-tappable 'Scheduled hours' rows. Other events are tappable and carry a status tag. 'Register time or absence' appears only when writing is allowed, and 'Confirm time' only when confirmation is allowed.
rules.given: A read-only user opens 9 September, which holds a public holiday named '' and one attendance event
rules.then: It shows a red 'Special day' header and the attendance row with its tag, and neither the Register nor the Confirm time button.
rules.parameters: Flags isWriteAvailable and isConfirmTimeAvailable are set by the caller (DayDetailFeature.swift:29-37). Empty day text: 'noActivityCalendar'.

rules.name: Confirm-time button needs the confirmTime permission
rules.plainEnglish: The list calendar shows the 'Confirm time' secondary button only when the user's permissions include confirmTime. A tap does nothing while the calendar buttons are disabled, for example when offline.
rules.given: A user with permissions [addTime, confirmTime] who is online
rules.then: The confirmation alert of the add-absence coordinator opens. A user without confirmTime sees no button at all.

rules.name: Register-event button needs a write permission
rules.plainEnglish: The list calendar shows the 'register event' button only to users who have addAbsence, addTime, absenceWrite or timeWrite. Read-only users do not see the button, and the button bar is removed.
rules.given: User A with [absenceReadOnly, timeReadOnly] and user B with [absenceWrite]
rules.then: User A sees no register button and the button container is removed (lines 568-575). User B sees the 'Register event' primary button.
rules.parameters: Write permissions: addAbsence, addTime, absenceWrite, timeWrite (ArrayExtensions.swift:19-21)

rules.name: Calendar is available only to users with an absence or time permission
rules.plainEnglish: The calendar feed loads only if the current user has at least one of six permissions: addAbsence, addTime, absenceReadOnly, timeReadOnly, absenceWrite or timeWrite.
rules.given: A user whose permissions are [expenseClaims] only
rules.when: The calendar feed tries to load
rules.then: The feed is disabled (the data source's isEnabled is false), nothing is fetched and the empty state appears. A user with [timeReadOnly] would get the feed.
rules.parameters: Calendar permissions: addAbsence, addTime, absenceReadOnly, timeReadOnly, absenceWrite, timeWrite. Enforced via CalendarFeedPagingControllerDataSource.isEnabled (DataSource/CalendarFeedPagingControllerDataSource.swift:23-25).

rules.name: Calendar tab titled 'Claims' for expense-only users
rules.plainEnglish: The tab is titled Calendar when the user has both absence and time permissions; otherwise Claims if they have expense claims; otherwise Calendar if they have absence or time.
rules.given: A user with absence permission and expense claims but no time permission
rules.then: The tab reads 'Claims' with the expense icon
rules.question: Should a user with absence permissions and expense claims really see the tab as 'Claims' rather than 'Calendar'?

rules.name: Only days of the displayed month show events and respond to taps
rules.plainEnglish: Leading or trailing days from the previous or next month appear in the grid but carry no events (CalendarViewUtils.swift:100), and tapping or long-pressing them does nothing.
rules.given: The September 2026 grid, which shows 31 August in its first row
rules.then: Nothing happens, and 31 August shows no events.

rules.name: Month cells show only absence and roster events, filtered by type
rules.plainEnglish: A day cell shows only absence-type and roster events. Confirmed-time and special-day entries never appear as cell events. An event without a filterable type is always shown, and one with a filterable type is hidden when the user has hidden that type.
rules.given: A day with an absence (filterable type 'attendance'), a roster shift and a confirmed-time entry, and the user has hidden attendance
rules.then: The cell shows only the roster shift.
rules.parameters: Filterable types: absence, attendance, supplement, unknown

rules.name: Agent offers Edit only when exactly one registration was predicted
rules.plainEnglish: After a prediction, the bot offers Confirm when at least one event is ready, Edit when exactly one event was predicted, and always Cancel. If no event is ready, the bot sends the follow-up messages for events that need editing instead of a summary.
rules.given: The agent predicts 2 vacations, both ready
rules.then: The buttons are Confirm and Cancel, with no Edit. With a single predicted vacation, the buttons would be Confirm, Edit and Cancel.

rules.name: Absences created in the chat can be opened only if they have a retrieval link
rules.plainEnglish: Tapping an event in the chat opens its detail only if it is a registered absence that has a retrieval link. Predicted, deleted and confirm-time events do nothing when tapped.
rules.given: A success summary with a registered vacation that has a retrieval link
rules.then: The absence detail view opens.

rules.name: Calendar hides entry types the user filtered out
rules.plainEnglish: Entries of type attendance, absence or supplement are hidden when the matching filter is off; entries of any other type are always shown.
rules.given: Show absence = off and a day with one 'absence' entry and one 'attendance' entry
rules.then: Only the attendance entry appears on that day and in its detail sheet
rules.parameters: Filters calendarShowAttendance / calendarShowAbsence / calendarShowSupplement, all default true (settingsReducer.ts:121-123)
rules.suspectedDefect: Filters apply to the grid and day sheet only; the list view (agendaItems, line 177-179) ignores them.

rules.name: Empty (draft) claims are fetched once per reset, filtered by the selected statuses
rules.plainEnglish: Before loading paged claims, the app fetches the claims with status 'empty' once per list reset, using the selected status filter, and adds them to the list.
rules.given: The claims list has just been reset with filter statuses ['open']
rules.when: data is fetched twice while scrolling
rules.then: the 'empty' claims request runs only on the first fetch, and the paged claims request runs on both
rules.parameters: AppConstants.ClaimStatus.empty = "empty"; the flag emptyClaimsShouldBeFetched is set back to true on reset()
rules.edgeCases: If the empty-claims request fails, the error is recorded and it is not retried until the next reset.

rules.name: Check-in and check-out send the device's local time with time zone
rules.source: EmployeeServices/Calendar/Sources/Calendar/Service/TimeService.swift:169-202 (plus 113-126 for status mapping; timestamp format at EmployeeServices/EmployeeCore/Sources/EmployeeCore/CoreFormatStyle.s…
rules.plainEnglish: Check-in uses PUT with the device's current time as ISO-8601 with its time zone offset. Check-out uses PUT to the server-provided checkout link with the same kind of timestamp. Each returns the new status: Idle, CheckedIn, Error or Conflict.
rules.given: The user taps Check in at 2026-09-28 08:02:10 in UTC+2
rules.then: the body is {localTime:'2026-09-28T08:02:10+02:00'} and the response status is 'CheckedIn'
rules.parameters: CheckinStatus values Idle, CheckedIn, Error, Conflict, unknown (Checkin.swift:11-19)
rules.edgeCases: The timestamp comes from the device clock, so a wrong clock records wrong worked time. A response without data throws an unexpected error.
rules.question: Should the server stamp check-in time instead of trusting the device clock?

rules.name: Delete is available only in edit mode and must be confirmed
rules.plainEnglish: The Delete button appears only when editing an existing registration; tapping it opens a warning dialog and the registration is deleted only if the user confirms.
rules.given: An existing vacation registration opened for editing
rules.when: The user taps Delete and then Delete in the warning dialog
rules.then: The registration is removed via the server's delete link and the 'deleted' post screen is shown
rules.edgeCases: New registrations never show Delete. Cancel leaves the record untouched.

rules.name: Absence save response lifecycle: Success, ValidationError, Error, ConfirmationRequired
rules.plainEnglish: Registering or updating an absence returns one of four outcomes: Success, ValidationError, Error or ConfirmationRequired. ConfirmationRequired returns a template that the user must confirm, using the server's save-button text, before it is saved.
rules.given: A vacation registration that would exceed the remaining balance
rules.when: the server answers statusCode 'ConfirmationRequired' with a template
rules.then: the app treats it as needing user confirmation (AbsenceRegistrationError.createAbsenceConfirmationRequired) rather than as saved
rules.parameters: statusCode values Error, Success, ValidationError, ConfirmationRequired; a response without a statusCode key fails to decode
rules.edgeCases: An unknown statusCode maps to .unknown. The same lifecycle applies to AbsenceUpdateResponse (lines 221-237).
rules.question: Is ConfirmationRequired only for balance overdraft, or also for other policy warnings? The server decides, and the merged app needs the same confirm step.

rules.name: Only input type, comment and sickness percentage survive a type change
rules.plainEnglish: When the user switches to another absence type, the entered input type and comment are carried over (plus certificate percentage if the new type is Sickness); all other entered values are discarded.
rules.given: A Vacation draft with comment 'Doctor' and project dimension '1001'
rules.when: The user switches the type to Sickness
rules.then: Comment 'Doctor' is kept, the dimension value is cleared
rules.edgeCases: For predictions from the Employee Agent the whole cache is cleared and saved values merged into the schema instead.

rules.name: Month grid: confirmed and approved timesheet entries are built separately
rules.plainEnglish: In the month grid, identical approver and confirmer dates produce one approved entry. Otherwise the grid shows an approved entry at the approver date (if any) and a separate pending 'confirmed' entry at the confirmer date (if any).
rules.given: Confirmer date 2026-09-15 and approver date 2026-09-30
rules.then: Two 'Timesheet confirmed' entries appear: approved on 2026-09-30 and pending on 2026-09-15. The list view would show one approved row.
rules.suspectedDefect: Equality uses exact Date values, so dates differing by seconds produce two entries. The list view compares with >= instead, so the two views can show different statuses for the same timesheet.

rules.name: Month grid knows only approved, rejected and pending request statuses
rules.plainEnglish: When an absence becomes a grid entry, its request status must exactly match 'approved', 'rejected' or 'pending'. Any other value becomes 'none', and the day-detail sheet then shows no status tag (DayDetailView.swift:18-34).
rules.given: An absence with requestStatus 'sent'
rules.when: The user opens its day in the month grid
rules.then: The event shows no status tag, while the list view labels the same absence 'Awaiting approval'.
rules.parameters: Grid statuses: approved (green tag), rejected (red tag), pending (blue tag), none (no tag)
rules.suspectedDefect: The match is case-sensitive and ignores statuses the list view handles, so the same absence can look 'Awaiting approval' in the list and unlabelled in the grid.
rules.question: Should the grid map sent, denied, notApproved, awaitingClearance, open, paid and canceled the way the list does? Right now they show no status in the day detail.

rules.name: List view: timesheet counts as approved when the approval date is on or after the confirmation date
rules.plainEnglish: In the list calendar, a confirmed timesheet shows as approved only when both dates exist and the approver's date is the same as or later than the confirmer's date. In every other case it shows as pending.
rules.given: Confirmer date 2026-09-15 and approver date 2026-09-10
rules.when: The confirmed-time row is shown in the list
rules.then: The status is pending. With approver date 2026-09-15 or later it is approved. With no approver date it is pending.

rules.name: Agent answer order: registrations first, then timesheet confirmation, then balances
rules.plainEnglish: If the agent's response contains registration predictions, only those are handled. Otherwise a confirm-time template is handled. Otherwise the balances text is shown.
rules.given: A response with 1 predicted vacation and a balances text
rules.then: Only the vacation prediction is offered for confirmation, and the balances text is not shown.

rules.name: How the agent reports registration results and failures
rules.plainEnglish: Successful registrations are listed in a success summary. A failed registration that needs confirmation (for example a future absence) becomes a confirm/cancel prompt. Other failures show the event description plus the error. If more than one failure would need buttons, the bot asks the user to register one by one. Once no buttons remain, the bot asks 'anything else?'.
rules.given: 3 predicted absences: 2 succeed, 1 fails with 'Overlaps existing absence'
rules.then: The chat shows a success summary listing the 2 absences, then an error message '<event description>\nOverlaps existing absence', then 'Anything else?'.

rules.name: A future absence needs explicit confirmation before it is registered again
rules.plainEnglish: When the server answers a registration with 'confirmation required' and a message, the bot shows that message as a warning with Confirm and Cancel. Confirm registers the template again (QuickResponseAction.confirmFutureAbsenceRegistration.swift:18-34). Without a message, the bot shows it as an error.
rules.given: Registering vacation for 2027-01-10 returns createAbsenceConfirmationRequired with the message 'This absence is far in the future. Continue?'
rules.then: The absence is submitted again and the result appears as a success or error message. Cancel discards it.

rules.name: Turning sync on saves the setting only if the sync run succeeds; turning it off always saves Off
rules.plainEnglish: Tapping the switch runs a full sync (birthdays and anniversaries) when it is not already on, and runs removal when it is on; a second tap is ignored until 2 seconds after the run finishes.
rules.given: calendarSync = sync_off
rules.when: The manager taps the switch and calendar permission is denied
rules.then: runSync returns false and the setting stays sync_off; had permission been granted, the setting becomes sync_all. From sync_all a tap always sets sync_off, even if removal fails
rules.parameters: Modes sync_off / sync_all (sync_birthdays and sync_anniversaries exist but the switch never uses them); lockout 2000 ms
rules.suspectedDefect: runSync returns true even when calendar creation or event saves fail (success flag is only used for the toast), so the setting can say 'On' when no events were written.

rules.name: Turning sync on deletes events that already exist for an employee instead of keeping them
rules.plainEnglish: When an employee already has a synced event, the code removes it rather than skipping it, even in sync_all mode.
rules.given: The 'Manager App - Birthdays' calendar still holds an event for employee E1 (for example after a reinstall reset the setting to Off)
rules.then: E1's existing birthday event is removed and no new one is created, so E1 ends up without a birthday event
rules.suspectedDefect: The else-if branch fires for foundEvents.length > 0 regardless of mode, so a re-sync with existing events removes them.
rules.question: Should turning sync on keep (or recreate) events that already exist for an employee, instead of deleting them?

rules.name: Turning sync off removes both Manager App calendars and clears the synced list
rules.plainEnglish: Mode Off (or no mode) deletes both 'Manager App' calendars from the device; birthdays-only deletes the anniversaries calendar and anniversaries-only deletes the birthdays calendar.
rules.given: Both 'Manager App - Birthdays' and 'Manager App - Anniversaries' exist
rules.then: Both calendars are removed from the device and the HRM synced-employee list is cleared
rules.parameters: sync_birthdays removes anniversaries calendar; sync_anniversaries removes birthdays calendar

rules.name: Synced events live in two dedicated device calendars
rules.plainEnglish: Birthdays go into a device calendar titled 'Manager App - Birthdays' and anniversaries into 'Manager App - Anniversaries'; each is created only if a calendar with that exact title does not already exist.
rules.given: No device calendar titled 'Manager App - Birthdays' exists
rules.then: A calendar 'Manager App - Birthdays' (owner 'VMM', source 'Manager', primary blue colour) is created; an existing calendar with that title is reused
rules.parameters: MANAGER_BIRTHDAYS_CALENDAR='Manager App - Birthdays'; MANAGER_ANNIVERSARIES_CALENDAR='Manager App - Anniversaries' (consts/constants.ts:119-120)

rules.name: Balance group categories: vacation, attendance, sickness, sick child
rules.plainEnglish: Balance groups belong to one of the categories vacation, attendance, sickness or sickchild. Any other value is treated as 'none'.
rules.given: The server sends a balance group with category 'overtime'
rules.then: its category is 'none'
rules.parameters: raw values vacation, attendance, sickness, sickchild, none; the unit id 'Hours' is recognised (EmployeeBalanceUnit.swift:21-23)

rules.name: A deleted absence is shown as struck through in the earlier success message
rules.plainEnglish: After the user deletes an absence created in the chat, the bot posts an 'event has been deleted' message. The earlier success summary is rewritten so that event shows struck through and can no longer be tapped, and the summary loses its buttons.
rules.given: A chat summary listing vacation 2026-10-05 that was created in the chat
rules.when: The user deletes that vacation from its detail view
rules.then: A new bot message says it was deleted, and the vacation line in the old summary appears struck through with no chevron.

rules.name: Switching from list to month view keeps the month last seen in the list
rules.plainEnglish: When the user switches from list to grid, the grid opens on the month at the top of the list.
rules.given: The list is scrolled to entries in June 2026
rules.when: The user switches to grid view
rules.then: The grid shows June 2026

rules.name: Only pending requests show a status tag in the day sheet
rules.plainEnglish: In the day details sheet, an entry whose request status is 'pending' gets an orange status tag; entries with status 'none' get no tag.
rules.given: A Vacation entry with requestStatus 'pending' and a Sickness entry with requestStatus 'none'
rules.when: The user opens the day sheet
rules.then: Vacation shows an orange 'pending' tag and Sickness shows no tag
rules.suspectedDefect: getApprovalStatusColors defines green for 'none', but it is never used; the feed has no approved or rejected status, unlike AbsenceRegistrationResource (Pending/Approved/Rejected/Cancelled).

rules.name: Server-requested confirmation before saving (future registration)
rules.plainEnglish: If the server answers a create or update with 'confirmation required' and a warning notification, the app shows the server's warning with its save-button text (default 'Confirm'); confirming resubmits the server-returned template, cancelling discards the pending confirmation.
rules.given: A vacation starting 2026-07-01 that the server flags with warning 'This is far in the future'
rules.then: A 'Future registration' alert shows the warning; tapping the server's button re-sends, Cancel returns to the form
rules.parameters: statusCode .confirmationRequired; style warning; update uses PUT to response.updateUrl
rules.edgeCases: If no warning notification is present nothing is thrown and the save is treated as successful. For updates a missing updateUrl also skips the confirmation.
rules.suspectedDefect: A confirmationRequired response without a warning notification is treated as success and the post-registration screen is shown although nothing was saved.

rules.name: Month data loading stops after 50 page requests or at the first error
rules.plainEnglish: To fill a month grid, the app keeps requesting past and future pages until the loaded range covers the month, no more pages exist, an error occurs, or 50 rounds have run. If the month lies wholly outside the loaded range, the app first restarts the feed at the month's start date.
rules.given: A month grid for 2026-09-01..2026-10-04 with a loaded feed range of 2026-09-10..2026-09-20
rules.then: The app requests past and future pages repeatedly until the range covers 2026-09-01 and 2026-10-04, stopping after at most 50 rounds or at the first error.

rules.name: Offline calendar hides the list and blocks registration and confirmation
rules.plainEnglish: When the device goes offline, the calendar hides the list and the register/confirm buttons, disables their actions and shows an offline placeholder. When the connection returns, the calendar restores them and reloads itself if it is visible.
rules.given: A user viewing the calendar list with the device online
rules.when: Connectivity is lost, then comes back
rules.then: On loss: the list is hidden, the offline text shows, and taps on Register or Confirm time are ignored. On return: the placeholder is removed, the buttons work again and the feed resets and reloads (lines 960-967). There is no offline queue of registrations.
rules.parameters: The offline text depends on permissions: expenseClaims gives the claims offline text; addAbsence or addTime gives the calendar offline text with 117 pt top padding (lines 54-75).
rules.suspectedDefect: In calendarViewModelDidFetchData (lines 234-242), the branch `else if isOffline && !isEmpty`, which would show 'cannot load more content', can never run because the `if isOffline` above it already caught that case.

rules.name: Closing the Employee Agent refreshes the start page and calendar
rules.plainEnglish: When the agent chat is closed, the app asks the start page and the calendar to reload so registrations made in the chat appear. The chat cannot be dismissed by swiping (line 61), and the conversation is kept only in memory, so it is lost on close.
rules.given: A user registered 2 absences in the agent chat
rules.then: The start page and calendar reload and show the 2 absences. Reopening the chat starts with only the introduction messages.
rules.question: Is losing the chat history on close intended, or should the conversation be kept for the session?

rules.name: Agent registers each predicted absence separately and in parallel
rules.plainEnglish: Confirming several predicted absences sends one create request per absence, all at once. Each succeeds or fails on its own, with no rollback of the others. An empty list sends nothing.
rules.given: The user confirms 3 predicted absences and the 2nd is rejected by the server
rules.then: Absences 1 and 3 are saved and 2 is reported as failed.
rules.suspectedDefect: The result handler force-unwraps registrationResponse.retrievalLink (CalendarChatBotViewModel.swift:509). A successful create that returns no retrieval link would crash the app after the absence was already saved.

rules.name: Several agent events needing attention are sent back for one-by-one registration
rules.plainEnglish: If exactly one predicted event needs editing, the bot shows the medical-certificate prompt for it. If more than one needs editing, the bot asks the user to register the events one by one.
rules.given: The agent predicts 2 sickness absences, both missing a required certificate date
rules.then: The bot replies with the 'register events one by one' message and offers no per-event edit.

rules.name: Confirm actions are locked while a submission is running
rules.plainEnglish: While a confirm action runs in the agent chat, the chat is marked busy and shows a loading message, so new prompts are refused. The day sheet likewise disables Confirm time while a confirmation is running (DayDetailView.swift:122-128). Sending any new chat message removes the previous quick-response buttons (lines 168-172).
rules.given: The user taps Confirm on 2 predicted absences
rules.when: The user tries to send another prompt before the result arrives
rules.then: The prompt is not sent, and the earlier Confirm button is gone, so the absences cannot be submitted twice.

rules.name: Team absence feed returns 'no absences' on any failure
rules.plainEnglish: The Start screen's 'who is absent' feed fetches 100 days forward from the month start for all managed employees across companies; any error (403, network, unknown environment, bad payload) is treated as an empty list, not an error.
rules.given: The feed endpoint returns 403 'User not allowed to do this operation'
rules.when: The Start screen loads the absence summary for from=2026-09-01

conflicts.difference: The year ranges differ. vmm offers 2 years back and 5 forward (September 2026 gives 2024-2031). me-ios offers 20 years each way (March 2025 gives 2005-2045).
The first day of the week differs. vmm always starts weeks on Monday (firstDay=1), whatever the locale. me-ios uses the locale's first weekday, so a Sunday-first locale starts the grid on Sunday.

Changing month works differently. In vmm swiping is turned off (enableSwipeMonths=false), so the user can only change month with the arrow buttons. In me-ios a swipe of at least 50 pt changes the month.

The access check differs. vmm shows the calendar only when it can find the employee's company tenant in the cached employee list; if not, it shows 'employee_calendar_load_error' and makes no permission check. me-ios requires one of addAbsence, addTime, absenceReadOnly, timeReadOnly, absenceWrite or timeWrite; an [expenseClaims]-only user gets the empty state.

The data in the grid differs. vmm shows fixed sample entries from mockData.ts (for example 'Sickness' on 7 October 2026 and a pending 'Vacation' on 8 October) for every employee. me-ios shows the real feed and drops any item whose type is not 'Absence' (for example 'Payslip'). The vmm behaviour looks like a defect.

How hours are shown: vmm prints the raw Hours property plus 'h' (Hours='7.5' gives '7.5h') and has no fallback. me-ios parses hours in the device locale, shows a compact duration ('7,5' gives '7 h 30 min'), and when there is no hours property it uses end minus start (09:00-11:30 gives '2 h 30 min').

Which properties drive the list description: vmm matches 'Hours' and 'Quantity' with exact case and has no percent case. me-ios matches 'hours', 'percent' and 'quantity' in any case, shows Percent absences as '50% <period>', formats time ranges in UTC ('08:00 - 12:00'), and gives a single-day Full Day absence no description.

Week numbers are on by default in vmm (calendarShowWeekNumbers=true) but off by default in me-ios (showWeekNumbers=false), so a new user sees week 40 on 2026-09-28 in vmm and no week number in me-ios.

The calendar shows different things. vmm shows every entry type that is not filtered out (attendance, absence, supplement) in the day cell and in the detail sheet. me-ios month cells show only absence and roster events and always leave out confirmed-time entries.

The filters differ. vmm has three filters (attendance, absence, supplement). me-ios also has a roster filter (showRoster=true), treats 'unknown' as a filterable type, and has a showLabels toggle (default false). vmm has no roster filter, no 'unknown' type and no labels toggle.

The apps may group the same entry under different filters. In me-ios an absence event can have the filterable type 'attendance', so hiding attendance hides it. In vmm the 'absence' entry type is controlled only by the Show absence filter. This needs checking: the same absence may disappear under a different toggle in each app.

The default calendar view differs: vmm opens in 'grid' (month) view (settingsReducer.ts:119), but me-ios opens in list view (UserPreferences.calendarViewMode default .list, CalendarContainerViewController.swift:52). So a first-time user sees the month grid in vmm and the list in me-ios.

Which request statuses get a tag in the calendar day view: vmm knows only 'none' and 'pending' and tags only pending, while me-ios also tags approved (green) and rejected (red). So an approved or rejected absence has a tag in me-ios and none in vmm.
The colour of the pending tag: orange in vmm, blue in me-ios.
